drivingQuestion: Must the court ask all seven interrogations even when some are pointless?
outcomeNote: Opens the baraita exchange; the Sages' reply follows in the next unit.

segments.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר. תַּנְיָא, אָמַר לָהֶם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לַחֲכָמִים: לְדִבְרֵיכֶם, מִי שֶׁבָּא וְאָמַר ״אֶמֶשׁ הֲרָגוֹ״, אוֹמֵר לוֹ ״בְּאֵיזוֹ שָׁבוּעַ?״, ״בְּאֵיזוֹ שָׁנָה?״, ״בְּאֵיזֶה חֹדֶשׁ?״, ״בְּכַמָּה בַּחֹדֶשׁ?״
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that «Rabbi Yosei says» they ask only on which day, at which hour, and in which place the event occurred, but not more. «It is taught» in a baraita the reasoning behind this dispute: «Rabbi Yosei said to the Rabbis: According to your statement» that the court asks all seven interrogations, when there is a witness «who came» to court «and said:» The accused «killed» the victim «last night,» should the judge «say to him» in his examination: «In which seven-year» period of the jubilee, «in which year, in which month, on which» day «of the month» did the accused murder the victim? What would be the purpose of asking these questions? It suffices that they ask him about the day, the time, and the place.
